title: An Inuit kayaker among the ice near a strait
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist); engraved by Edward Finden
description: A hunter paddles a kayak through loose ice, with other boats and a group of figures visible farther off. The printed caption is too degraded to transcribe in full, but its second line ends in the word "Strait", consistent with the ships' passage into Hudson Strait early in the voyage.

title: The Fury and Hecla secured in their winter harbour
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist); engraved by Edward Finden
description: The two ships lie moored to fast ice off a snow-covered shore with sails furled and rigging bare for the winter. In the foreground several men stand on the ice near a flagstaff and sledge dogs, evidently marking out or surveying the harbour at Winter Island.

title: An Iglulingmiut woman beside a store of meat and skins
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: A woman in a fur-hooded amautik sits with a bowl of food beside a rack and stone platform hung with cut meat, skins, and other winter provisions. The plate has no legible printed caption in this scan, but the scene matches Parry and Lyon's descriptions of domestic life at Winter Island.

title: Two seals resting on the ice
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: Two seals hauled out on a sheet of shore ice, drawn for the natural-history record of the voyage. No legible caption survives on this scan to give the species by its English or scientific name.

title: Inuit hunters sealing at breathing-holes in the ice
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist); engraved by Edward Finden
description: A hunter lies prone on the ice with a harpoon poised over a seal's breathing-hole while other hunters wait nearby, illustrating the patient still-hunting method that supplied much of the Iglulingmiut winter diet, as Parry and Lyon repeatedly described.

title: A hunter waiting beside a seal's breathing-hole
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: A single hunter crouches on the snow beside a seal's breathing-hole with his harpoon and coiled line laid ready, a companion image to the other sealing plates in this volume.

title: Hunters approaching seals on the ice
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: One hunter creeps toward a seal with harpoon and coiled line in hand while a second figure stalks upright farther off, showing two of the approaches to seal-hunting on open ice that Parry and Lyon recorded at Winter Island.

title: An Inuit dog-sledge and its team
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: A fan-hitched team of dogs draws a loaded sledge with its driver, seen in profile -- one of several plates in which Parry and Lyon documented Iglulingmiut sledging equipment and technique in detail during the first wintering.

title: A shore camp with a tent structure, a dog, and a sledge
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist); engraved by Edward Finden
description: A framed, canvas-walled tent or hut stands on the snow beside a man in fur dress, a harnessed dog, and a sledge with coiled line. The engraved caption is too faint in this scan to transcribe with confidence about the exact place and date shown.

title: Winter costume of the Esquimaux: man, woman, and child
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: A man and woman stand in heavy fur winter dress with a small child beside them, while in the distance other figures, a dog team, and a sledge cross the snow. This is one of a pair of costume plates in the volume documenting Iglulingmiut clothing in careful detail.

title: Summer costume of the Esquimaux: man with a spear, and a woman
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: A man in caribou-skin clothing stands holding a long spear or staff, paired with a woman in similarly heavy dress on bare ground -- the companion "summer dress" plate to the winter costume portrait elsewhere in the volume.

title: A settlement of snow houses, with drying racks and dogs
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: Several snow houses and a raised meat-drying rack stand on the sea ice with dogs and a fur-clad figure among them, a winter-village scene most likely showing the Iglulingmiut settlement near the ships' second wintering.

title: Inuit hunters spearing caribou at a water crossing
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist); engraved by Edward Finden
description: Several hunters, at least one in a kayak, spear swimming caribou as the animals cross a river or lake, with a camp of tents on the shore beyond -- the annual caribou hunt that Parry and Lyon watched and recorded near Igloolik.

title: Coastal profile views: Cape Bylot and the entrance to Duke of York Bay
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: Panoramic outline sketches of the coast as seen from the ship, part of a large folding plate of coastal profiles used for pilotage. The labelled strips on this leaf cover Cape Bylot and the north shore of the entrance to Duke of York Bay, on Southampton Island.

title: Coastal profile views: Cape Welsford, Duke of York Bay, Cape Deas Thomson, and northern Southampton Island
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: A row of labelled coastal-profile sketches from the same folding plate, showing Cape Welsford, the entrance to Duke of York Bay, Cape Deas Thomson, Cape Bylot, and the northern part of Southampton Island as seen from Frozen Strait near Passage Island -- visual aids for recognising the coast from the deck of the ship.

title: Coastal profile views: Cape Penrhyn and the mouth of the Strait of the Fury and Hecla
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: Further strips from the folding plate of coastal profiles, labelled with Cape Penrhyn and the mouth of the Strait of the Fury and Hecla, the strait Parry's ships tried and failed to force in 1822.

title: Coastal profile views: Liddon Island, the Narrows, and the Strait of the Fury and Hecla
creator: G. F. Lyon (artist)
description: Coastal-profile strips labelled Liddon Island, the Narrows seen from east and west, and views of the Strait of the Fury and Hecla taken from Whyte Inlet and from Fire Rock -- the innermost part of the strait that blocked Parry's passage west.

title: General Chart shewing the track of H.M. Ships Fury and Hecla, on a voyage for the discovery of a North-West Passage, 1821-22-23
creator: John Walker (engraver)
description: The volume's summary chart of the whole voyage, plotting the ships' track from Hudson Strait through Foxe Basin to Igloolik and the Strait of the Fury and Hecla against the wider geography from Baffin Bay to Hudson Bay, with the coasts newly discovered by this and the preceding expedition shaded to show what had been added to the map.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at sea, June 1821
description: Monthly table of air temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in June 1821, during the outward passage toward Hudson Strait.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at sea, July 1821
description: Monthly table of air temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in July 1821, as the ship worked north and west through Foxe Channel.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at sea, August 1821
description: Monthly table of air temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in August 1821, in the final weeks before the ships reached Winter Island.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, September 1821
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury in September 1821, shortly before the ships entered winter quarters.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, November 1821
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in November 1821. Registers like this one are among the earliest sustained instrumental weather series kept in Foxe Basin and on the Melville Peninsula.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, December 1821
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in December 1821, in the depth of the first Arctic wintering.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, January 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in January 1822, among the earliest sustained instrumental weather series kept in this part of the Arctic.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, February 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in February 1822, during the coldest weeks of the first wintering.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, March 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in March 1822, the month in which Iligliuk drew her chart for Parry and Lyon.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, April 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in April 1822, as the days lengthened toward the spring thaw.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, May 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in May 1822, not long before the ships worked free of the harbour ice.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Winter Island, June 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Winter Island in June 1822, the last full month of the first wintering before the ships put to sea again.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at sea, August 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in August 1822, as the ships worked north through Foxe Basin toward the Strait of the Fury and Hecla.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at sea, September 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, sea-water temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at sea in September 1822, during the attempt to force the Strait of the Fury and Hecla.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Igloolik, December 1822
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in December 1822, early in the ships' second Arctic wintering.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Igloolik, January 1823
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in January 1823, part of one of the earliest sustained instrumental weather series kept on the Melville Peninsula.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Igloolik, March 1823
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in March 1823, during the second Arctic wintering.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Igloolik, April 1823
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in April 1823, as the second wintering drew toward its end.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Igloolik, May 1823
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in May 1823.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, at Igloolik, July 1823
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury at Igloolik in July 1823, shortly before the ships left their second winter quarters.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, August 1823
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury in August 1823, as the ships worked their way out of Foxe Basin at the end of the voyage.

title: Abstract of the meteorological journal kept on board H.M.S. Fury, September 1823
description: Monthly table of temperature, barometric pressure, and prevailing winds recorded aboard H.M.S. Fury in September 1823, on the homeward passage through Hudson Strait.

title: Note on the pronunciation of Esquimaux words, prefacing the vocabulary
creator: William Edward Parry
description: Parry's explanatory note on how he rendered Inuktitut sounds in English spelling, with worked examples of each vowel combination, followed by remarks on how Iglulingmiut speakers often answered a question about an object's name with the name of its material instead -- citing "neitiek" (seal) and "amia" (skin) given in place of "poo-a-look" (mitten).

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Air to Bite
creator: William Edward Parry
description: The opening page of Parry's Inuktitut-English vocabulary, compiled with George Francis Lyon at Winter Island and Igloolik, running alphabetically from "Air, or weather" (See-la) to "Bite, he does" (Ka-o-loke-poke). An early, careful record of the Iglulingmiut dialect by outsiders who lived among its speakers for two winters.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Bristles to Conjuror
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Bristles" to "Conjuror, or Sorcerer," including everyday nouns and verbs recorded from Iglulingmiut speakers during the voyage.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Drunk to Father-in-law
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Drunk, he is" to "Father (or mother) in-law," part of Parry and Lyon's word-list of the Iglulingmiut dialect.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Give to Heart
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Give" to "Heart," continuing the alphabetical word-list compiled during the second voyage.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Jacket to Lamp of stone
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Jacket, under" to "Lamp of stone," including the word "Igloo" for a snow house and "Cappee-tegga" for a stone lamp -- terms central to Iglulingmiut winter life.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Lamp-trimmer to Nail of the finger
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Lamp-trimmer (sometimes of asbestos)," glossed as "Tat-ko," through household, family, and natural-world terms to "Nail of finger, or toe." A representative page of Parry and Lyon's careful record of the Iglulingmiut dialect.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Ornament to Rib
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Ornament of brass or copper worn on the forehead by Esquimaux women" to "Rib, small," continuing the alphabetical word-list.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Seal-hole to Skins of deer
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Seal-hole" ("Toolemak") to "Skins of deer, made into a blanket," recording the specialised terms of the winter hunt.

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Spear for large seal to Sweat
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Spear for large seal" and "walrus and whale" through "Swallow-pipe of an animal," "Swan," and "Sweat, he does."

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Too, And, or Also to Very, or Extremely
creator: William Edward Parry
description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary running from "Too, And, or Also" and "To-day" through "Vaccinium uliginosum" (bog blueberry), "Valley, or Low-land," and "Very, or Extremely."

title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Whistle to Young
creator: William Edward Parry
description: The closing page of Parry's Inuktitut-English vocabulary, running from "Whistle, he does" and "White, or any light colour" to "You" (singular and plural) and "Young, he is."

title: Esquimaux names of places, from Southampton Island to Ormond Island
creator: William Edward Parry
description: The opening page of Parry's list of Inuktitut place names, recording Iglulingmiut names for Southampton Island ("the land of Sead-ler-meoo"), Repulse Bay, Lyon Inlet, Winter Island ("Ne-yu-ning Eit-du-a"), and other places the expedition charted, set beside the English names given by the British. A direct record of Indigenous geography and naming, gathered from the same Iglulingmiut community that produced Iligliuk's chart.

title: Esquimaux names of places, from Quilliam Creek to Autridge Bay
creator: William Edward Parry
description: The closing page of Parry's list of Inuktitut place names, including Liddon Island and Amherst Island (both called "Seag-glur-ru-ok") and Whyte Inlet ("Ewee-ta-oke-toke"), ending the volume with "THE END."
